born 25th July 1931, Pimlico; ran for the A.A.A. in Billy Morton's Mile, Dublin, 24 July 1957; footballer with Wimbledon and Kingstonian, a year on Tottenham Hotspur's amateur books; joined Belgrave May 1955 after a thigh injury ended football; 3rd in 1955 club 1 mile championship in 4:27; ran Invitation 800m, White City, Whitsun 1956; 5th in Invitation 800m, Whitsun British Games, White City 1956, in 1:52.3; won Middlesex mile championship June 2nd 1956; won Heathfield trophy 880 yards in 1:55.9; 4:11.8 for 3rd in Brockman Trophy mile; 5th in Southern Championships 1 mile 1956; 1:52.8 club 880 yards record in A.A.A. Championships heats 1956; won 1956 club 880 yards in 1:56.8; 7th in 800m at Karlstadt in 1:52.7; won Vancouver Trophy 800 metres, 2nd in L.C.C. mile 1956; regained Middlesex Mile title 1958; best mile 4:10.6 equalling club record; won 1958 club 880 yards, mile and three miles (14:25); ran road relays incl. London - Brighton into the sixties; married Pam 1960; began 'O' levels at 30, gained 8 passes; 2:07:59 in Finchley '20' 1973; Harlow Marathon debut 142nd in 2:55:36 at 42; 2:53 at Harlow 1974; Club Champion with 2:52 in Road Runners Marathon, Milton Keynes, July 1975; 2:47.35 at Harlow October 1975

Back Page:
Gerard Deegan (number obscured) of Waterford and Belgrave H put some remarkable cross country talent behind him in this six mile race held over a heavy five-lap course at Fermoy, County Cork on February 6th. Bernie Ford (Aldershot, Farnham & Dist) was the winner in 29:09 with Gerard 11 seconds down in 2nd place but comfortably ahead of John Wild (Camb & Col), Jos Hermans (Netherlands), Danny McDaid (Tirconal), the Tuck Twins (Camb & Col), and Julian Goater and Dave Bedford (both Shaftesbury). Another Belgravian, John Phelan, racing for Donore, was 23rd.

An even more notable scalp in Gerard's collection this season is that of National Champion Brendan Foster, whom he had beaten a few weeks earier by ten yards at Mallusk, Belfast.

photos.c: Above: Not only did Marlon Dickson pick up an All-England medal while running for London in the 4x100m, he also set new Club Record figures for our U15 100m by running 11.70.

Front page: ... And to think that we used to know him as "little Marlon". Shown here at the McDonald's YA League at Peterborough matching strides out of the blocks with Blackheath's Mark Findlay, Marlon Dickson had a great 1994 season. At 15 years of age he set personal bests of 11.36 and 23.1 and ran anchor leg for our U17M record breaking 4x100 quartette. He looks set to make a name for himself in 1995 when he remains in the same age-group and has already clocked 7.1 for an indoor 60m at the 'Palace'. Each season so far he has chopped 4/10ths off his 100m best. Another improvement like that would give him 10.96. Phil Goedluck's U17M record? - 10.96!
